main_text.p: solutum est. Quo perfecto aliam fossam parem fodit, non multum a priore distan-ctam, spectantem ad mediterranea: addiditque duas praterea alias istis[?] similes, & circumpositas, ita ut totum opus fos-sionis fieret quadrangulum, omnesque ejus partes muniit vallo acutis: & post val-los fossas altas vallumq; castrense duxit.

Ea vero parte, qua Carthaginem spectabat, murum etiam extruxit xxv stadio-rum longitudine, altitudine pedum xii, prater propugnacula & turres, qua per intervalla muro imminebant: latitudo seu crassities muri dimidium altitudinis aquabat. In medio turris erant altissima tecta quadruplici fastigio ligneo, un-de despicere licebat ea, qua in urbe fie-rent. His operibus totius exercitus la-bore absolutus intra dies noctesque vi-ginti quatuor, militibus vicissim nunc arma tenentibus nunc opus facientibus, nec cibum nec somnium nisi necessarium capientibus, in his castris collocavit co-pias: praebuitque ei hoc opus tum castro-[illegible, ~3 letters]rum usum, tum munitionum contra hoste[illegible, ~2 letters] extensarum. Hinc enim erumpens [illegible, ~8 letters] meatum, qui à terra iis afferebatur Carthaginiensibus adimebat. [illegible, ~3 letters]Nam hac sola cervice exceptâ reliqua omnis urbs undiq; circumluebatur. Atque hac prima, ac maximè samis malorumque causa ob-sessis

page.notes: The right margin carries small marginal notes that are too faint and fragmentary to read; they are marked as illegible at their positions, and their exact placement is approximate. The word "istis" (line 4) is uncertain and marked [?]; the printed form appears to read "istis" but may be "iisdem". The word at the line end after "erumpens" overlaps a marginal note and cannot be read. The paragraph ends mid-sentence with "ob-" and "sessis" on the last line; there is no catchword or signature visible.
